findings.description: publicly_accessible = true gives the MySQL RDS instance a public IP and internet-resolvable endpoint, so the database listener is reachable from the public internet whenever the attached security group permits it. Databases holding application data should reside in private subnets with no public route.

storage_encrypted = false leaves the database volume, snapshots, automated backups and read replicas unencrypted, so anyone with access to the underlying storage or a snapshot can read the catalog data.

The EC2 user_data script writes the database password (var.password), username and endpoint in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc and the instance user data. User data is retrievable via instance metadata and the EC2 API, and the file sits under the web root, leaking live DB credentials to anyone who can read them.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", so compromise of the role-assuming instance yields full control of all S3 data, every EC2 instance and every RDS database in the account, including backup deletion and privilege escalation. This is far beyond least privilege.

The instance is launched with iam_instance_profile = catalog_app_profile, which carries the wildcard s3:*/ec2:*/rds:* policy, while it is a publicly reachable web server running a PHP application. Compromise of the web tier therefore escalates directly to account-wide cloud privileges.

MySQL port 3306 is open to the entire VPC CIDR rather than restricted to the application security group, so any workload or compromised host in the VPC can connect to the database, widening the attack surface beyond the intended app tier.
The database security group allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting unrestricted data exfiltration and outbound command-and-control if the database tier is compromised.
The master username is hardcoded to the well-known default "admin", easing credential guessing against a database whose endpoint is publicly resolvable.

The lifecycle block ignores changes to the password, so a rotated or remediated credential written to configuration will never be applied to the instance, preventing credential rotation from taking effect.
